strings: This rock is filled with pockets of breathable air.
A flexible, superconducting insulated cable for heavy-duty power transfer.
It's coarse and rough and gets everywhere.
A square piece of iron standing on four metal legs. It can not move.
Flooring that shows its contents underneath. Engineers love it!
A high-capacity superconducting magnetic energy storage (SMES) unit.
A warning sign which reads 'HIGH VOLTAGE'.
A one meter section of regular pipe.
This rock is filled with pockets of breathable air. It has metal struts to protect it from mining.
A Prism-brand path illumination device. It is anchored in place and glowing steadily.
A coil of insulated power cable.
A heavy wooden box, which can be filled with a lot of ores or boulders
A control terminal for the area's electrical systems.
A huge chunk of iron used to separate rooms.
A trusty station intercom, ready to spring into action even when the headsets go silent.
You sit in this. Either by will or force.
It's a storage unit for emergency breath masks and O2 tanks.
All you need to destroy those pesky weeds and pests.
She's the queen of bees, BZZ BZZ!
A scaffold for bees to build honeycomb on.
A small wall mounted cabinet designed to hold a fire extinguisher.
Pull this in case of emergency. Thus, keep pulling it forever.
What did I say about leaning on the glass tables? Now you need surgery.
A dropper. Holds up to 5 units.
A syringe that can hold up to 15 units.
Some type of shrubbery. Known for causing considerable economic stress on designers.
You can't tell if this is real grass or just cheap plastic imitation.
Basic railing meant to protect idiots like you from falling.
A charging dock for energy based weaponry, PDAs, and other devices.
Emergency air-tight shutter, capable of sealing off breached areas. This one has a glass panel. It has a mechanism to open it with just your hands.
A machine that monitors atmosphere levels. Goes off if the area is dangerous.
This cute little guy just loves the taste of insulated electrical cables. Isn't he adorable?
A stack of various papers, childish scribbles scattered across each page.
A Trauma Response Activation Medibot. It seems overwhelmed.
Do not apply fire to this. Rumour says it burns easily.
Smack it with a gavel when the assistants get rowdy.
Order, order! No bombs in my courthouse.
An underfloor disposal pipe with a sorting mechanism.
A little bit of nature contained in a pot.
It's a storage unit for fire-fighting supplies.
It's Officer Beepsky! Powered by a potato and a shot of whiskey, and with a sturdier reinforced chassis, too.
A small electronic device able to ignite combustible substances.
These gloves are cheap knockoffs of the coveted ones - no way this can end badly.
Has a valve and pump attached to it.
A sink used for washing one's hands and face. Passively reclaims water over time.
Emergency air-tight shutter, capable of sealing off breached areas. It has a mechanism to open it with just your hands.
A huge chunk of reinforced metal used to separate rooms.
A one meter junction that connects regular and heat-exchanging pipe.
A one meter section of heat-exchanging pipe.
Different from the Middle Ages version.
A high-visibility vest used in work zones.
Used for pulsing wires to test which to cut. Not recommended by doctors. You can activate it in-hand to locate the nearest APC.
Come on Lady Luck, spawn me a pair of sunglasses.
A catwalk for easier EVA maneuvering and cable placement.
A lightweight support lattice. These hold our station together.
Now you see me, now you don't...
Light and airtight plastic flaps made to keep the cold room cold and the warm room warm.
It's Sergeant-At-Armsky! He's a disgruntled assistant to the warden that would probably shoot you if he had hands.
Sturdy exterior hull plating that separates you from the uncaring vacuum of space.
A tank full of industrial welding fuel. Do not consume.
For when it all gets too much to bear. Do not taunt.
An equipment shop for miners, points collected at an ore redemption machine can be spent here.
Damn, they better have the /tg/ channel on these things.
A thick resin surface covers the floor.
They look like the remains of something... alien. They have a strange aura about them.
The spawner of the keg on the station. Special stuff on Beer Day and St. Patrick's Day.
A sign with the Nanotrasen logo on it. Glory to Nanotrasen!
A small screen which the AI can use to present itself.
Used to view and edit personnel's security records.
People with ropes around their necks don't always hang.
Oh, I'm a cowboy. On a steel horse I ride. I'm wanted (wanted), dead or alive
Used to recolor floors and walls. Can be removed by the janitor.
A wrench with common uses. Can be found in your hand.
Do jump on it, it can take it.
It has some unsavory stains on it...
A heavy duty blast door that opens mechanically.
An outlet for the pneumatic disposal system.
A window that is reinforced with metal rods.

A guide to the exhibit, explaining how recent developments in mindshield implant and cloning technologies by Nanotrasen Corporation have led to the development and the effective immortality of the 'perfect man', the loyal Nanotrasen Employee.
Soft velvet carpeting. Feels good between your toes.
It's a floor-mounted device for projecting holographic images.
An adapter which allows pipes to connect to other pipenets on different decks.
A compact medical bed. This emergency version can be folded and carried for quick transport.
A double sided angled mirror for reflecting laser beams.
A pump that moves gas by pressure.
A one meter section of regular pipe used to connect pipenets over pipes.
A standard Nanotrasen-licensed newsfeed handler for use in commercial space stations. All the news you absolutely have no use for, in one place!
A warning sign which reads 'RADIOACTIVE AREA'.
Heavy duty mechanical shutters with an atmospheric seal that keeps them airtight once closed.
All engineering related spawners go here

A guide to the drone shell dispenser, detailing the constructive and destructive applications of modern repair drones, as well as the development of the incorruptible cyborg servants of tomorrow, available today.
A large duffel bag for holding tools and hats.
A painting machine that can be used to paint PDAs and trim IDs. To use, simply insert the item and choose the desired preset.
Crack it open, inhale the musk of its pages, and learn something new.
Go back. Go back. Go back. Can you operate the elevator.
Indicates what floor the elevator is at and which way it's going.
Bluespace technologies on the application of bureaucracy.
Contains all the paper you'll never need.
It's a normal black ink pen.
An advanced autopainter preprogrammed with several paintjobs for airlocks. Use it on an airlock during or after construction to change the paintjob.
A lightbulb you can walk on without breaking it, amazing.
A warning sign which reads 'SECURE AREA'.
A flexible, superconducting insulated multilayer hub for heavy-duty multilayer power transfer.
\"In case of emergency, please use the stairs.\" Thus, always use the stairs.
Heats or cools gas in connected pipes.
A radio beacon used for bot navigation.
A custom security console with added access to the labor camp network.
Contains everything you need for your fishing trip.
It's a storage unit for athletic wear.
It's your run-of-the-mill wall clock showing both the local Nanotrasen Standard Time and the galactic Treaty Coordinated Time. Perfect for staring at instead of working.
A soft and fluffy pillow. You can smack someone with this!
It's a storage unit for rad-protective suits.
The HS-452. Installed in the 2550s by the Nanotrasen Hygiene Division, now with 2560 lead compliance! Passively replenishes itself with water when not in use.
A small rack for storing coffeemaker cartridges.
